ELMALILI:82:8-19/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r1.claim: One parsing makes rakabaka depend on fi ayyi sura, treats ayyi as an adjective meaning ‘any,’ ma as emphatic, and sha’a as describing sura; it renders God as forming a person in whichever form He wills.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r1.anchor: “Seni muhtelif suretlerden dilediği herhangi bir surette terkib ve tasvir eyledi.”

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r2.claim: A second parsing makes ayyi conditional and rakabaka future: God may form a person in any shape or remove him from human beauty into the ugliest forms, warning against delusion.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r2.anchor: “seni herhangi bir surette dilerse terkib ve tasvir eder, dilerse o güzel insan kılığından çıkarır da en çirkin suretlere kor,

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r3.claim: A third parsing attaches adalaka to fi ayyi sura and treats ma sha’a rakabaka as a separate relative, indefinite, or conditional clause; it can mean balancing or shaping at will, or reshaping if God wills.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r3.anchor: Bu takdirde meal “seni herhangi bir surette denkleştirdi” yahut “evirdi çevirdi, dilediği gibi seni terkib etti”

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r4.claim: All three readings are possible and sound; sura may mean forms varying in beauty or in beauty and ugliness, covering physical and moral traits and resemblance to relatives.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r4.anchor: Bu mânaların hepsi de muhtemil ve sahihtir.

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r5.claim: The range of forms includes resemblance to parents or relatives, color, height, sex, health, righteousness, intelligence, and their opposites, in physical and moral qualities.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r5.anchor: anaya babaya ve sâir akrabaya müşabehet ve adem-i müşabehet, renk, uzunluk, kısalık, erkeklik dişilik

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r6.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Abu Rabah al-Lahmi a Prophetic report in which God brings a child’s ancestral lineages into view after the semen settles in the womb.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r6.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem şöyle buyurdu: “Öyle deme, nutfe rahimde istikrar edince Allah teâlâ onunla Âdem beynindeki her nesebi ihzar

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r7.claim: The report points to a conditional sense in ayyi or ma.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r7.anchor: Birisi, اَيِّ yahut مَا’da şartiyet mânası.

ELMALILI:82:8-19/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r8.claim: It also points to inherited traits: semen can carry characteristics of lineages passed down from ancestors since Adam.
ELMALILI:82:8-19/r8.anchor: neseblerin, hususiyetlerin her birini ihtivâ edebilir.

ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r1.claim: The report’s third implication is that God’s will, not nature, is the effective agent in hereditary traits.
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r1.anchor: fâ‘il-i müessir tabiat değil, Allah teâlâ’nın meşiyyeti olduğunun isbâtıdır.

ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r2.claim: Remote ancestors’ traits can prevail over those of parents, showing God’s will governs varied natures and forms; hereditary values exist and matter, but judgment rests solely with God.
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r2.anchor: ana baba gibi yakın ataların hususiyetlerine tâ Âdem’e kadar varan uzak atalardan birinin hususiyeti galebe ettirilmesi

ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r3.claim: One should seek nearness to God through faith, gratitude, obedience, and good works, earning future worthiness and protection from punishment rather than presuming on grace.
ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r3.anchor: iman ve şükran ile tâate ve hayır amellere sarılmakla olur.

ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.claim: Asad reports that some authorities date the surah to early Mecca, while others consider it more likely to belong to the last group of Meccan revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.anchor: others regard it as more probable that it belongs to the last group of Meccan revelations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.claim: Al-Infiṭār is the counterpart of al-Takwīr, sharing its intrinsic and extrinsic form, style, meanings, and opening cataclysm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.anchor: great similarity between the intrinsic and extrinsic form, style and meanings of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.claim: Both sūrahs address rich, arrogant Quraysh who ignored the warnings because they trusted their castles and edifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.anchor: The real addressees of both sūrahs are the rich and arrogant among the Quraysh who were turning a deaf ear to the warnings of the Qur’ ān just because they thought that no one would be able to break into their castles and edifices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.claim: Al-Takwīr reasons from the Qur’an’s authenticity, source, revelation, and bearer; its rejecters cannot distinguish radiant dawn from murky night.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.anchor: the bearer are all pure and upright.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.claim: Al-Infiṭār instead reasons from God’s creativity, power, wisdom, justice, and mercy: signs of power and mercy in humans entail a coming day of reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.claim: Resurrection is no difficulty for God: if first creation was easy, creating again is no harder, and the coming day is certain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.anchor: creating again be difficult for Him?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.claim: God’s present respite for criminals gives them time to reform; those who refuse have no excuse or justification at Judgment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.claim: Divine delay does not mean words and deeds are hidden: angels have been assigned to everyone to record everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.anchor: This delay from God should not mislead people to think that their words or deeds are hidden from Him. He has deputed His angels on every person who are noting down each and everything.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.claim: Human formation displays divine power, wisdom, mercy, and justice, showing that Judgment is possible and that human existence has purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.anchor: With reference to the grandeur of divine attributes of power, wisdom, mercy and justice found in the formation of a human being a reminder is sounded that no one should think that the Day of Judgement is beyond the power of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.claim: God’s power, creativity, care, and wisdom in creating humanity show that He acted purposefully and will hold people accountable, resurrecting and judging them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r1.anchor: power, creativity, thoroughness and wisdom in creating

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.claim: The creation vocabulary spans making or sketching and creating, then perfecting; the verses thus allude to humanity’s initial and final stages of formation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r2.anchor: “to make a sketch of something” and “to create something”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r1.claim: The diversity of human forms shows that God created each person in a distinct mould.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r1.anchor: each person was made in a different mould with different looks

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r2.claim: The word for proportion refers to balance and proportion, which the author connects to humanity’s creation in the finest mould.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r2.anchor: balance and proportion mentioned in the verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.claim: Humanity reflects God’s brilliant creativity and must pass through tests to its appointed fate; refusal to face that responsibility merits punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r3.anchor: a reflection of the brilliant creativity of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.claim: The human midpoint among creations makes people worthy of vicegerency and the status of the middle community; fulfilling this duty merits the eternal kingdom of Heaven.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r4.anchor: is worthy of being made the vicegerent of God on earth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r5.claim: The variety of faces and forms demonstrates God’s creative skill, since people were shaped differently without difficulty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r5.anchor: each person was made in a different mould with different looks

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r6.claim: The One who creates people effortlessly will distinguish the righteous from wrongdoers and raise humanity again with equal ease.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p219/r6.anchor: will raise up mankind once again without the slightest of difficulty.

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.claim: God fitted the body's limbs according to wise designs, varying beauty and ugliness, and height and shortness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11.anchor: ركب أعضاءك على الوجوه الحكمية { فى أى صورة ما شآء } ، من الحسن والقبح ، والطول والقصر

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r12.claim: Alternatively, “image” means attribute and fī means ʿalā; God formed each person in the attribute He willed, whether felicity or misery, faith or disobedience.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r12.anchor: الصورة هنا بمعنى الصفة ، و ( في ) بمعنى ( على ) ؛ فيكون معناه : على أي صفة شاء ركبك ؛ من السعادة أو الشقاوة ، والإيمان أو المعصية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r1.claim: The phrase can connect with ‘He formed you’: God assembled people in any form, known or unknown, including beasts, birds, and other animals.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r1.anchor: { في أي صورة } من الصور التي تعرفها والتي لا تعرفها من الدواب والطيور وغير ذلك من الحيوان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r2.claim: A report from Mālik b. al-Ḥuwayrith says that at conception the man’s fluid spreads through the woman’s veins and nerves; on the seventh day God gathers every vein reaching back to Adam and recites this verse. Al-Biqāʿī notes the transmitters are trustworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r2.anchor: روى الطبراني في معاجمه الثلاثة برجال ثقات عن مالك بن الحيرث رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r3.claim: The report establishes that people are permanently enslaved to God; whoever casts off that bond and relies on himself perishes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r3.anchor: فتحَرر بهذا الإنسان رقيق رقا لازما , ومن خلع ربقة ذلك الرق اللازم وكل إلى نفسه فهلك

NAHHAS:v5p169/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p169/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p169/r2.claim: ما is extra in the construction.

NAHHAS:v5p169/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p169/r3.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p169/r3.claim: Mujahid says God formed the person in the image of a father, mother, uncle, or maternal uncle.
NAHHAS:v5p169/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد في صورة أب أو أم أو عم أو خال

TABATABAI:82:1-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:1-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:1-19/r1.claim: Humanity's finest form and all its arrangements depend on the generous Lord's governance; humans have no hand in them.
TABATABAI:82:1-19/r1.anchor: والجميع ينتهي إلى تدبير الرب الكريم لا صنع للانسان في شيء من ذلك

TABATABAI:82:19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:19/r2.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:82:19/r2.claim: Al-Qummi explains that God could have composed a person in a form other than the one he has.
TABATABAI:82:19/r2.anchor: قال لو شاء ركبك على غير هذه الصورة

TABATABAI:82:19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:19/r3.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:82:19/r3.claim: Al-Majma transmits the same explanation from Ja'far al-Sadiq in a disconnected report.
TABATABAI:82:19/r3.anchor: ورواه في المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام مرسلا

TABRISI:82:1-19/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19/r2.claim: In one grammatical analysis, ma is emphatic and the meaning is that God formed the person in whichever form He chose, tall, short, or otherwise; rakabaka is coordinated with ʿadalaka with a conjunction omitted.
TABRISI:82:1-19/r2.anchor: يجوز أن تكون ما مزيدة مؤكدة والمعنى في أي صورة شاء ركبك إما طويلا وإما قصيرا

TABRISI:82:1-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19/r3.claim: Alternatively, ma is conditional: God formed the person in whatever form He wished; the interrogative phrase must attach to an omitted verb, not rakabaka or ʿadalaka, following Sibawayhi's rule about moving an object before a conditional clause.
TABRISI:82:1-19/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما في معنى الشرط والجزاء فيكون المعنى في أي صورة ما شاء أن يركبك فيها ركبك

TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r1.claim: In a report transmitted through al-Rida and his forefathers, the Prophet tells a man that the child may resemble any lineage between the sperm and Adam, in accordance with God's forming in whatever image He wills.
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r1.anchor: " عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لرجل:

TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة وأبو صالح
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r2.claim: Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may form a person in any created shape, even a human, donkey, or ape.
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r2.anchor: في أي صورة ما شاء من صور الخلق ركبك إن شاء في صورة إنسان وإن شاء في صورة حمار وإن شاء في صورة قرد عن عكرمة وأبي صالح

TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r3.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r3.claim: Al-Sadiq says God could have formed a person differently but made him in the best form, unlike any animal.
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r3.anchor: لو شاء ركبك على غير هذه الصورة والمعنى أنه سبحانه يقدر على جعلك كيف شاء ولكنه خلقك في أحسن تقويم

TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r4.claim: A further interpretation lists possible forms by sex, build, beauty, and height: male or female, stout or thin, handsome or ugly, tall or short.
TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r4.anchor: في أي صورة شاء من ذكر أو أنثى أو جسيم أو نحيف حسن أو دميم طويل أو قصير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:8-19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:8-19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:8-19/r1.claim: God composed each person in the form He willed, whether tall or short, handsome or ugly.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:8-19/r1.anchor: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك } إما طويلا؛ وإما قصيرا؛ وإما حسنا؛ وإما قبيحا.

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r1.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r1.claim: Some understand the verse as God choosing a particular human form for each person.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r1.anchor: Some take this verse to indicate the manner in which God chooses a particular human form for each individual

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r2.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r2.claim: Others understand that God can assemble humans in the form of other animals, presumably as punishment, as in the transformation of the people addressed at 2:65.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r2.anchor: Others take this to mean that God can assemble human beings in the form of other animals

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.speaker: Qu and R
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.claim: Verses 7–8 can refer to inner qualities, such as states of faith or disobedience, rather than outer form.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r3.anchor: Vv. 7–8 can also be taken to imply the inner qualities rather than the outer form, thus referring to states of faith or disobedience

STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.claim: The verses can also refer to states of felicity or wretchedness, commonly understood as salvation and damnation.
STUDYQURAN:82:8/r4.anchor: which are commonly understood as referring to states of damnation and salvation

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r5.claim: Mujahid says God formed the human in the likeness of a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} [الانفطار: 8] قال: في أي شبه: أب أو أم

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r6.speaker: إسماعيل عن سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r6.claim: Ismail reports that God could form a person in a dog's or donkey's image if He willed.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r6.anchor: عن سفيان، عن إسماعيل، في قوله: {ما شاء ركبك} [الانفطار: 8] قال: إن شاء في صورة كلب

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r7.claim: Abu Salih gives the possible images as a pig or a donkey.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r7.anchor: عن سفيان، عن إسماعيل، عن أبي صالح، {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} [الانفطار: 8] قال: خنزيرا أو حمارا

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r8.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r8.claim: Ikrima says God could form a person as a monkey or a pig.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} [الانفطار: 8] قال: إن شاء في صورة قرد

TAB-FULL:v24p178/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r9.claim: The Prophet tells a questioner that, once semen settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between it and Adam, so resemblance may be to either parent; he invokes this verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p178/r9.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عندها: " مه، لا تقولن هكذا، إن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم

THALABI:v10p147/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p147/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p147/r3.claim: Mujahid says the chosen resemblance may come from a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
THALABI:v10p147/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: في أي شبه أب أو أم أو خال أو عم.

THALABI:v10p147#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p147#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p147#2/r1.claim: In a report about a child’s resemblance, the Prophet says that once semen settles in the womb God brings the lineages back to Adam and may form the child as a human, donkey, monkey, dog, or pig.
THALABI:v10p147#2/r1.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تقل هكذا إن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أحضر الله كل نسب بينهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r1.claim: Mujāhid takes the image to mean the form of a father, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: في صورة أب، أو خال، أو عم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r2.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet says that once the sperm settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between it and Adam; al-Wāḥidī cites it as support for Mujāhid's view, without grading it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r2.anchor: ما روى أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال (¬7): "وإذا استقرت النطفة في الرحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r1.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say the image may be tall, short, handsome, or otherwise; on their reading, ما is an emphatic extra particle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r1.anchor: وذكر الفراء (¬1)، والزجاج (¬2) قولا آخر: "في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك" إما طويلا، وإما قصيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r2.claim: In al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj's explanation, ما in ما شاء is an additional particle used for emphasis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r2.anchor: و"ما" في قوله: "ما شاء" صلة مؤكدة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r3.claim: Muqātil, also joined by Abū Ṣāliḥ, says God could have formed the person in a nonhuman shape such as a dog, donkey, pig, or ape.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r3.anchor: ومقاتل (¬5): يقول إن شاء ركبك في غير صورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq parses ما conditionally: in whatever form God wills to form the person, He forms him in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون "ما" في معنى الشرط، والجزاء، فيكون المعنى: في أي صورة ما شاء أن يركبك فيها ركبك. ذكره أبو إسحاق

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.claim: The creation and formation described in verses 7–8 expose the ingratitude of people who owe their bodily and mental faculties, and all other blessings, to their Lord yet are misled into denial and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r3.anchor: insanın insan olarak varlık alanına çıkışındaki yaratıcı rolü dile getirilmekte; böylece insanın, hayatı boyunca her an yararlanmakta olduğu diğer bütün nimetlerden de önce bedensel ve zihnî melekelerle donatılıp düzgün bir insan olarak dünyaya gelişini kendisine borçlu bulunduğu rabbi hakkında

BURHAN:v1p429#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r2.claim: Sīn in ‘sūra’ marks something that encloses an object from outside, while ṣād in ‘ṣūra’ marks what contains it within.
BURHAN:v1p429#2/r2.anchor: فبالسين ما يحصر الشيء خارجا عنه وبالصاد ما تضمنه منه

ITQAN:v4p534#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p534#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p534#2/r1.claim: A weak-chain report says the Prophet corrected a father who guessed whether a child would resemble either parent: after the sperm settles, God establishes the lineages reaching back to Adam; he glossed ‘in whatever form He willed’ as ‘He shaped you.’
ITQAN:v4p534#2/r1.anchor: بسند ضعيف من طريق موسى بن علي بن رباح عن أبيه عن جده أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham objects that rebuke is not apparent in the fashioning verse, the standing of people, or “then its explanation is upon Us”; proposed rebukes are strained, especially after the long separation in the third example.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r1.claim: In representation (tamthīl), one image appears as a single image seen first in a mirror and then directly; explicit simile presents two actual images.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r1.anchor: انك بالتمثيل في حكم من يرى صورة واحدة إلا انه يراها تارة في المرآة وتارة على ظاهر الأمر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r2.claim: Abstract nearness and distance require a sensory model: a man can be distant in status yet near in generosity only by recalling the moon’s physical distance and near light.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r2.anchor: فلا يتصور معنى كون الرجل بعيدا من حيث العزة والسلطان قريبا من حيث الجود والإحسان حتى يخطر ببالك وتطمح بفكرك إلى صورة البدر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r3.claim: Visible qualities of a flower can be perceived directly, without simile; comparison adds a second image to the one already seen.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r3.anchor: فإنك لا تفتقر في معرفة كون النرجس وخرطه واستدارته وتوسط أحمره لأبيضه إلى تشبيهه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r4.claim: In the abstract comparison, the branch does not possess the original’s actual quality; it only seems present, like a second person in a mirror that vanishes when the correspondence ends.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r4.anchor: لا تجد في الفرع نفس ما في الأصل من الصفة وجنسه وحقيقته ولا يحضرك تمثيل الأصل على التعيين والتحقيق وإنما يخيل إليك انه يحضرك ذلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r1.claim: The paired-sun poem aims to astonish listeners with an event outside experience and ordinary custom.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r1.anchor: معلوم أن القصد أن يخرج السامعين إلى التعجب لرؤية ما لم يروه قط ولم تجر العادة به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r2.claim: To sustain that wonder, the poet boldly asserts the impossible as fact, disregarding expected denial and the appearance of falsehood.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r2.anchor: حتى يجترىء على الدعوى جراءة من لا يتوقف ولا يخشى إنكار منكر ولا يحفل بتكذيب الظاهر له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r3.claim: The sun-shading, two-suns, and other poems share only the broad device of asserting an impossible sight; their distinct specific wonders mean this shared idea is not plagiarism.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r3.anchor: الاشتراك بينها عامي لا يدخل في السرقة إذ لا اتفاق بأكثر من أن أثبت الشيء في جميع ذلك على خلاف ما يعرفه الناس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r4.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s image of suns appearing from the beloveds’ homes without an east is a distinct version of the impossible-sun conceit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r4.anchor: وهكذا قول المتنبي ( كبرت حول ديارهم لما بدت منها الشموس وليس فيها المشرق )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r5.claim: Another distinct wonder has the moon walk toward a person and lions embrace a man; the marvel lies in those specific violations of ordinary experience.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r5.anchor: قوله ولم أر قبلي من مشى البدر نحوه العجب من أن يمشى البدر إلى آدمي وتعانق الأسد رجلا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r6.claim: A reverse technique assigns a subtle, distinctive feature of the comparison’s source to the target, making the simile or metaphor seem to disappear.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r6.anchor: أن تنظر إلى خاصية ومعنى دقيق يكون في المشبه به ثم تثبت تلك الخاصية وذلك المعنى للمشبه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r1.claim: A true metaphor works like a genuine loan: the borrowed name must confer its full use on the recipient, as clothing is lent for the borrower to wear as its owner would.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r1.anchor: شرط المستعار أن يحصل للمستعير منافعه على الحد الذي يحصل للمالك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r2.claim: In “Zayd is a lion,” the name Zayd prevents lion from applying to him with the unrestricted force of its literal name; this is unlike a complete transfer of the noun.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r2.anchor: الاسم في قولك زيد أسد لا يقع من زيد ذلك الموقع من حيث أن ذكره باسمه يمنع من أن يصير الاسم مطلقا عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r3.claim: With “I meant a gazelle,” the noun is understood in its ordinary animal sense, not as naming a woman; Jurjānī uses this to show what unrestricted application of a name entails.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r3.anchor: وجدنا الاسم في قولك عنت ظبية يعقل من إطلاقه أنك قصدت الجنس المعلوم ولا يعلم انك قصدت امرأة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r1.claim: Figurative attribution does more than assign a property to an undeserving branch: the comparison implicitly attributes it to the rightful original as well.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r1.anchor: وإنه ينظر من هذا إلى ذاك وإثباته ما أثبت للفرع الذي ليس بمستحق يتضمن الإثبات للأصل الذي هو المستحق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r2.claim: A man can be likened to a lion in courage only by first recognizing courage as one of the lion’s most characteristic and predominant qualities.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r2.anchor: لا تقدر على أن تشبه الرجل بالأسد في الشجاعة ما لم تجعل كونها من أخص أوصاف الأسد وأغلبها عليه نصب عينيك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r3.claim: Attributing an action to a cause presupposes the rational principle that real action belongs to a capable agent; without that basis, the causal assertion would be literal rather than figurative.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r3.anchor: من أن لا فعل على الحقيقة إلا للقادر لأنه لو كان نسب الفعل إلى هذا السبب نسبة مطلقة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r4.claim: Jurjānī excludes the disbelievers’ literal claim that time alone destroys from his discussion of figurative causal attribution.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r4.anchor: ولحق بنحو قول الكفار وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر وليس ذلك المقصود في مسئلتنا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r5.claim: Saying that a knife cuts or a sword kills only forms a coherent attribution when the listener also imagines the actual agent wielding the instrument.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r5.anchor: قطع السكين وقتل السيف فإنك تعلم انه لا يقع في النفس من هذا الإثبات صورة ما لم تنظر إلى إثبات الفعل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r6.claim: Saying that a prince struck coins or built a wall by command still depends on recognizing the direct workers as the actual performers.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r6.anchor: ضرب الأمير الدراهم و بنى السور لا تقوم في نفسك صورة لإثبات الضرب والبناء فعلا للأمير بمعنى الأمر به

AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.claim: The adjacent identical kāf consonants may assimilate; he also describes when to leave them unassimilated according to whether the first or second letter is vowelled.
AKHFASH:v2p570/r3.anchor: فادغمت لأنهما حرفان مثلان. والمثلان يدغم احدهما في صاحبه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r4.claim: Some read the verse as transmigration of souls, but Ibn Qutayba rejects that reading and says the address is not to one particular person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r4.anchor: وتأول قوم في قوله تعالى: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.claim: The address is generic, as in O human, striving toward your Lord; God formed and proportioned people in whatever forms He chose, in beauty, ugliness, whiteness, blackness, dark complexion, or redness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5.anchor: كما يقول القائل: يا أيها الرجل، وكلكم ذلك الرجل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r6.claim: He links the variety of chosen human forms and colors to the signs in the creation of the heavens and earth and the variation of human languages and colors.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r6.anchor: ونحوه قوله: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r7.claim: Some say God's utterance is not real speech but the production of meanings, and treat much Quranic speech metaphorically, like saying a wall spoke when it leaned.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r7.anchor: وذهب قوم في قول الله وكلامه: إلى أنه ليس قولا ولا كلاما على الحقيقة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r4.claim: Kallā in the next clause means matters are not as the addressee has deluded himself.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r4.anchor: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك (8) كلا بل تكذبون بالدين (9) [الانفطار: 8، 9] ، أي ليس كما غررت به

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r1.claim: One analysis attaches في أي صورة to ركبك, treats ما as extra, and makes شاء an adjective of صورة; ركبك explains فعدلك rather than joining it with a فاء.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن يتعلق ب " ركبك " و " ما " مزيدة

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r2.claim: On that analysis, God placed the person in the form his will specified, across such dimensions as beauty, ugliness, height, shortness, and sex.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r2.anchor: والتقدير: فعدلك: ركبك في أي صورة من الصور العجيبة الحسنة التي شاءها. والمعنى: وضعك في صورة اقتضتها مشيئته: من حسن وقبح وطول وقصر وذكورة وأنوثة

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r3.claim: A second analysis treats the prepositional phrase as a circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted element: he assembled you present in one of the forms.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r3.anchor: الثاني: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال، أي: ركبك حاصلا في بعض الصور

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r4.claim: A third reported analysis attaches في أي صورة to عدلك, but the author objects that interrogative أي must lead its clause and cannot have a preceding governor.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r4.anchor: الثالث: أنه يتعلق بعدلك، نقله الشيخ عن بعض المتأولين، ولم يعترض عليه، وهو معترض: بأن في " أي " معنى الاستفهام، فلها صدر الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari senses wonder in أي, glossing the phrase as God proportioned the person in a wondrous form; the author says this still does not license a preceding governor.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r5.anchor: وهذا لا يحسن أن يكون مجوزا لتقدم العامل على اسم الاستفهام

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r6.claim: The correct grammatical position is that even interrogative forms used for confirmation cannot have their governor precede them; the same restriction applies to the resembling exclamatory كيف and أنى and to كم الخبرية.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r6.anchor: والصحيح أنه لا يجوز، وكذلك لا يجوز أن يتقدم عامل " كم " الخبرية عليها لشبهها في اللفظ بالاستفهامية فهذا أولى

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r7.claim: If في أي صورة attaches to عدلك, ما is accusative with شاء, apparently as a verbal noun: God assembled you as he willed, in a fine arrangement.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r7.anchor: وعلى تعلقها ب " عدلك " تكون " ما " منصوبة ب " شاء "

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows ما to be extra or conditional; either way the clause modifies صورة with an omitted return pronoun (ركبك عليها), and في attaches to ركبك.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون " ما " زائدة، وأن تكون شرطية، وعلى الأمرين: الجملة نعت ل " صورة " ، والعائد محذوف، أي: ركبك عليها. و " في " تتعلق ب " ركبك "

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r9.claim: Another view gives the clause no syntactic position because في attaches to one of the two verbs, شاء or ركبك; the interrogative precedes ما, its proper position.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r9.anchor: وقيل: لا موضع للجملة؛ لأن " في " تتعلق بأحد الفعلين، والجميع كلام واحد، وإنما تقدم الاستفهام على " ما " هو حقه. قوله: " بأحد الفعلين " يعني: شاء وركبك

SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r10.claim: The passage yields three analyses of ما: extra, conditional with an omitted answer, or accusative as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r10.anchor: وتحصل في " ما " ثلاثة أوجه: الزيادة، وكونها شرطية، وحيئنذ جوابها محذوف، والنصب على المصدرية، أي: واقعة موقع مصدر

ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r1.claim: If mā is an emphatic extra particle, the sense is that God formed you in whichever shape He wished, tall or short, attractive or otherwise.

ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, mā is conditional: in whatever shape He chose to form you, He formed you in it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما في معنى الشرط والجزاء، فيكون المعنى في أي صورة ما شاء أن يركبك فيها ركبك

ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.claim: Because both sides of human nature are willed by God, Asad says there is no inherent moral conflict between flesh and spirit.
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n5/r2.anchor: both these aspects of the human condition are - as stressed in the next verse - God-willed and, therefore, morally justified.

NASHR:v1p301/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r1.speaker: أبو الطيب وابن مقسم عن التمار عن رويس
NASHR:v1p301/r1.claim: Abu al-Tayyib and Ibn Muqsim, both transmitting through al-Tammar from Ruways, pronounce the preceding assimilation case clearly rather than assimilating it.
NASHR:v1p301/r1.anchor: رواه أبو الطيب وابن مقسم كلاهما عن التمار عنه بالإظهار

NASHR:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p301/r2.claim: The text lists fourteen places of Ruways's optional assimilation: three in al-Baqara, then examples in al-Araf, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, al-Naml, al-Zumar, al-Rum, al-Shura, al-Najm, and al-Infitar.
NASHR:v1p301/r2.anchor: واختلف عنه أيضا في أربعة عشر حرفا وهي ثلاثة في البقرة فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم

NASHR:v1p302/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r3.speaker: الأهوازي عن رويس
NASHR:v1p302/r3.claim: Al-Ahwazi reports Ruways assimilating rakibka kalla; al-Mabhaj includes this reading.
NASHR:v1p302/r3.anchor: الأهوازي إدغام ركبك كلا، وهو الذي في " المبهج "

NASHR:v1p302/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r4.speaker: الباقون عن رويس
NASHR:v1p302/r4.claim: Other transmitters from Ruways show all these passages; both assimilation and clear pronunciation are sound transmissions from him.
NASHR:v1p302/r4.anchor: وروى الباقون عن رويس إظهار جميع ذلك، والوجهان عنه صحيحان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r3.claim: Mujahid, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say God formed each person in a likeness of a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل: في أي شبه من أب أو أم أو خال أو عم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r4.claim: A report says that when semen settles in the womb, every vein between it and Adam is brought forth, then the Prophet recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r4.anchor: وجاء في الحديث: أن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أحضر كل عرق بينه وبين آدم ثم قرأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ offers another reading: God could form a person as a human, a beast, or another animal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r5.anchor: وذكر الفراء قولا آخر: "في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك" إن شاء في صورة إنسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.claim: The phrase means God formed the person in whichever form He chose; ma may be extra or conditional, with rakabaka as its answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.anchor: أي ركبك في أي صورة شاءها، و { ما } مزيدة وقيل شرطية، و { ركبك } جوابها

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.claim: The prepositional phrase attaches to adalaka.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.anchor: و الظرف صلة { عدلك } ، وإنما لم يعطف الجملة

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.claim: This sentence explains the preceding word adalaka, which is why it is not coordinated with the preceding sentence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.anchor: وإنما لم يعطف الجملة على ما قبلها لأنها بيان لعدلك

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r9.speaker: علي بن رباح
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r9.claim: A report through Musa ibn Ali ibn Rabah says God fashions the child in a form from the ancestral line between the parents and Adam after the fluid settles in the womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r9.anchor: وأخرج البخاري في تاريخه وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن شاهين وابن قانع والطبراني وابن مردويه من طريق موسى بن علي بن رباح

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r10.speaker: مالك بن الحويرث
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r10.claim: A good-chain report says the man’s fluid runs through the woman’s veins and nerves; on day seven God brings forth ancestral lines to Adam and fashions the child, then the Prophet recites the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r10.anchor: وأخرج الحكيم الترمذي والطبراني وابن مردويه بسند جيد والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات عن مالك بن الحويرث

DURR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: A report tells of an Anṣari newborn who was black; the Prophet said each parent has ninety-nine veins, which all ask God for resemblance when a child is formed.
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: وأخرج الحكيم الترمذي عن عبد الله بن بريدة أن رجلا من الأنصار ولدت له امرأته غلاما أسود

DURR-FULL:v8p439/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r2.claim: Mujahid says God may form a person handsome or ugly, resembling a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن مجاهد {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} قال: إما قبيحا وإما حسنا

DURR-FULL:v8p439/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r3.claim: Abu Salih says God may form a creature as a donkey, pig, horse, or human.
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر والرامهرمزي في الأمثال عن أبي صالح {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك}

DURR-FULL:v8p439/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r4.claim: Ikrima says God may form a creature as a monkey or in a pig’s image.
DURR-FULL:v8p439/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة في قوله: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r1.claim: Ayy originally asks which thing distinguishes one item from its peers in some respect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r1.anchor: اعلم أن أصل { أي } أنها للاستفهام عن تمييز شيء عن مشاركيه في حاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r2.claim: Frequently the question conventionally expresses wonder at the quality of what follows; the sense of perfection arises from usage, not from ayy itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r2.anchor: والاستفهام بها كثيرا ما يراد به الكناية عن التعجب أو التعجيب من شأن ما أضيفت إليه { أي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r3.claim: Ayy functions semantically as an adjective of an indefinite noun, either as a descriptive adjective or as a genitive attached to an indefinite, as here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r3.anchor: و { أي } هذه تقع في المعنى وصفا لنكرة إما نعتا نحو : هو رجل أي رجل ، وإما مضافة إلى نكرة كما في هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r4.claim: “In whatever image” may attach to the sequence “created you, proportioned you, and made you upright,” with a pause after the phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r4.anchor: فيجوز أن يتعلق قوله : { في أي صورة } بأفعال خلقك ، فسواك ، فعدلك ) فيكون الوقف على { في أي صورة }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r5.claim: Alternatively, the phrase attaches to “assembled you”; “whatever He willed” interrupts it, so the pause comes after “made you upright.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق بقوله { ركبك } فيكون الوقف على قوله { فعدلك } ويكون قوله { ما شاء } معترضا بين { في أي صورة } وبين { ركبك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r6.claim: Both parses mean that God formed the human in whatever complete, wondrous image He chose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r6.anchor: والمعنى على الوجهين : في صورة أي صورة ، أي في صورة كاملة بديعة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r7.claim: The preposition fī is figurative, meaning association; the wondrous image is a circumstantial state and is pictured as a container to show how fully it characterizes the addressee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r7.anchor: و { في } للظرفية المجازية التي هي بمعنى الملابسة ، أي خلقك فسواك فعدلك ملابسا صورة عجيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r8.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun, accusative as an absolute object; its clause has an omitted object, “He willed it,” so the sense is that He formed the structure He chose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p176/r8.anchor: و { ما } يجوز أن تكون موصولة ما صدقها تركيب ، وهي في موضع نصب على المفعولية المطلقة و { شاء } صلة { ما } والعائد محذوف تقديره : شاءه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r7.speaker: جمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r7.claim: The majority attach في to ركبك, covering ugly or beautiful, deformed or sound forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r7.anchor: ذهب الجمهور إلى أن في متعلقة ب ركبك، أي في قبيحة أو حسنة أو مشوهة أو سليمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r8.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r8.claim: Some attach it to عدلك, meaning God formed the human into any image.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r8.anchor: وذهب بعض المتأولين إلى أن المعنى فعدلك في أي صورة: بمعنى إلى أي صورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r9.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r9.claim: Another view makes it a threat: God could form the human as a donkey, pig, or other creature.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r9.anchor: وذهب بعض المتأولين إلى أن المعنى: الوعيد والتهديد، أي الذي إن شاء ركبك في صورة حمار أو خنزير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r10.anchor: وما في قوله: ما شاء، زائدة فيها معنى التأكيد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r11.claim: تركيب means composing and joining one thing to another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r11.anchor: والتركيب والتأليف وجمع الشيء إلى شيء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r12.speaker: خارجة عن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r12.claim: Kharija reports Nafiʿ’s reading ركبك كلا with assimilation of one kāf into another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r12.anchor: وروى خارجة عن نافع: «ركبك كلا» بإدغام الكاف في الكاف،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r1.claim: Mujahid says the form may resemble any of the child’s paternal or maternal relatives: father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: في أي شبه أب أو أم أو خال أو عم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r2.claim: A report says God brings together in the womb the lineages between the child and Adam, explaining why resemblance is not limited to either parent; Ibn Kathir says it would settle the verse if sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عندها: "مه. لا تقولن هكذا، إن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says this report’s isnad is not established: Mutahhar ibn al-Haytham was called matruk by Abu Sa‘id ibn Yunus, and Ibn Hibban criticized his reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r3.anchor: ولكن في الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله، إن امرأتي ولدت غلاما أسود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r4.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra in both Ṣaḥīḥs, a man asks about his dark-skinned newborn; the Prophet compares it to a camel whose color reflects an ancestral trait, suggesting a bloodline cause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله، إن امرأتي ولدت غلاما أسود؟. قال: "هل لك من إبل؟ "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r5.claim: Ikrima says God could form a person in the likeness of an ape or a pig.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r5.anchor: قال عكرمة في قوله: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} إن شاء في صورة قرد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r6.claim: Abu Ṣāliḥ says God could form a person like a dog, donkey, or pig.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r6.anchor: وكذا قال أبو صالح: إن شاء في صورة كلب، وإن شاء في صورة حمار، وإن شاء في صورة خنزير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir reads these reports as showing God’s power to make the embryo a hideous animal, while by power, gentleness, and forbearance He forms it upright, balanced, complete, and beautiful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r7.anchor: ومعنى هذا القول عند هؤلاء: أن الله، عز وجل، قادر على خلق النطفة على شكل قبيح من الحيوانات المنكرة الخلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r8.claim: Qatada’s point is that God is fully capable of forming the embryo in such an unusual animal shape.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: {في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك} قال: قادر-والله -ربنا على ذلك

MUQATIL:82:6-13/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r4.claim: God assembled the human in whatever form He willed; He could have made him in a form other than human.
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r4.anchor: يعني لو شاء ركبك في غير صورة الإنسان

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.speaker: النبي عن موسى بن علي عن أبيه عن جده
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.claim: Musa ibn Ali reports through his father and grandfather that the Prophet said that, once the sperm settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between that person and Adam, in connection with “in whatever image He wished, He composed you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r2.anchor: عن جده قال: قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.speaker: عكرمة وأبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.claim: Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may compose a person in a human, donkey, ape, or pig form.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة وأبو صالح: { في أى صورة ما شآء ركبك

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.speaker: مكحول
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.claim: Makhul says the form may be male or female, as God wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r4.anchor: وقال مكحول: إن شاء ذكرا، وإن شاء أنثى

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.claim: Mujahid says the image is a likeness inherited from a father, mother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or another relative.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: «في أي صورة» أي في أي شبه من أب أو أم أو عم أو خال أو غيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.claim: The preposition “fi” attaches to rakkabaka, not ʿadalaka; on the light reading one says ʿadaltu ila, not ʿadaltu fi. Al-Farra therefore rejected that reading when he attached “fi” to ʿadalaka.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r6.anchor: و «في» متعلقة ب «ركبك»، ولا تتعلق ب «عدلك»، على قراءة من خفف لأنك تقول عدلت إلى كذا، ولا تقول عدلت في كذا

QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.claim: Mā may be an emphatic extra particle, yielding “in whatever image He wished”; alternatively it is conditional, allowing the image of an animal as well as a human.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r7.anchor: و «ما» يجوز أن تكون صلة مؤكدة أي في أي صورة شاء ركبك. ويجوز أن تكون شرطية أي إن شاء ركبك
